narrative.overview:
Every app is one rounded glass frame floating over a full-bleed photo that runs on behind it to the screen edge. Type sits on the photo: one thin Gilda Display title per screen with one word in the app's accent, under a tracked uppercase kicker with em-dashes. Chrome is glass; anything you read (lists, running text, forms) sits on a solid or near-opaque card. Charcoal marks the current thing (nav pill, current row, primary action) and the one key-facts card per screen. Colour comes from the photo; the UI is white glass, charcoal and warm greys plus one accent.

These are working tools (Operate mode). Ambition shows as precision: dense data that survives the worst case, motion that confirms and stays out of the way, contrast checked against the darkest pixel a photo can put under text.
keyCharacteristics: One frame over one photo; Notes swaps the photo for a blurred colour field and puts the editor on a solid white card.
Glass for chrome, solid for reading.
One display title per screen, one accent word in it, nowhere else.
One charcoal key-facts card per screen (Notes is the exception: no key-facts card; its only charcoal surfaces are the current tree item, the primary pill and the code block).
Pills everywhere: controls, bars, nav. Round icon buttons. Light, quiet DM Sans for everything that isn't a title.
Light theme (D9), except the night stage: an app with worlds (Creative) shows each world as a dark banner in the world night, its glow on the accent word. Components use roles, never hues.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: One accent per app, from rosemary, slate, heather or lagoon. No orange, ember or amber app accent (Rue, round 1). The rule covers app accents only: Life's ochre and orange aspect colours are category colours, not accents.

rules.name: The Colour from the Photo Rule
rules.body: The UI adds no colour of its own beyond the accent. Content palettes are content: they never stand in for the accent and never carry a state alone.

rules.name: The Roles not Hues Rule
rules.body: Components reference role tokens only (`check-slop` fails on colour literals). A dark theme later is another set of role values.

rules.name: The One Weight Rule
rules.body: Gilda Display is never bold, never italic, never asked for another weight. `base.css` sets `font-synthesis: none`; `<strong>` inside a Gilda title is a bug.

rules.name: The Accent Word Rule
rules.body: A title carries one accent word, `<em class="accent-word">`, except count titles, where the accent may cover the whole count phrase ("This week", "16 titles", "7 / 18 done"). No accent on list items, labels, card heads or buttons.

rules.name: The Kicker Rule
rules.body: Kicker parts are written in sentence case and joined by em-dashes that CSS draws (`li + li::before`), so a wrapped line starts with "— part" and never ends on a dash. Uppercase comes from CSS, never from the source text.

rules.name: The Glass for Chrome Rule
rules.body: Glass holds controls, never running text or lists. Plain `--surface-glass` sits on the frame or a scrim; over bare photo use `--surface-glass-strong`. Reading goes on `--surface-card` or `--surface-raised`.

rules.name: The One Charcoal Card Rule
rules.body: One card per screen is `[data-surface="inverse"]`, with `--shadow-lift` and no glass. It holds the key facts, not decoration.

rules.name: The Night Scrim Rule
rules.body: On the night stage (`.app[data-world][data-stage="night"]`) every scrim stop becomes the world veil. `--world-veil` is the floor under every line of type, checked over a white pixel; each world sets its own strength so light photos stay bright, not murky.

dos: Do start every screen from the skeleton in `DESIGN-reference.md`: frame over photo, head on the photo, cards overlapping its lower edge.
Do put running text, lists and forms on `--surface-card` / `--surface-raised`; glass only for chrome.
Do keep exactly one display title, one accent word and one charcoal key-facts card per screen.
Do mark every dark surface `data-surface="inverse"` and every solid card that holds secondary buttons `data-surface="solid"`.
Do use the four motion hooks and nothing else: `data-press`, `data-pill`, `data-settle`, `data-confirm-line`.
Do check new colour pairs in `contrast-pairs.json` and run `node scripts/check-contrast.mjs` (every accent and every world).
Do render every screen with the worst-case data in `DESIGN-reference.md` before calling it done.
donts: Don't box the screen's main photo small in a card, or replace a missing image with a gradient.
Don't put text on plain glass over a busy photo; it needs `--surface-glass-strong` or a solid surface.
Don't bold, italicise or reweight Gilda Display.
Don't use orange, ember or amber as an app accent, or use a content palette colour as the accent.
Don't animate `backdrop-filter`, `filter` or layout properties; don't use `transition: all`.
Don't remove the focus outline without a replacement ring.
Don't make Delete the primary button.
Don't reveal an action or information on hover only.
